title: Star formation region Lupus 3
caption: Star-forming region Lupus 3, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope and the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Snaking across this wide view is a dark cloud of dust, lit by the brilliant light of newly formed stars. This dense cloud is Lupus 3, a star-forming region where very hot stars are being born from collapsing masses of gas and dust.

Stars begin life inside clouds like this one. Where the gas and dust are packed densely enough, gravity pulls material inward until it becomes hot and dense enough for a new star to ignite. The cloud looks dark because its dust blocks the light of the stars behind it, while the young stars nearby shine brightly beside it.

The picture was assembled from images taken with two ESO telescopes, the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope and the VLT Survey Telescope. According to ESO, the result is the most detailed image yet made of this region, giving astronomers a sharp look at a place where stars are forming.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was assembled from data taken with ESO's VLT Survey Telescope and the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope. The filter list also includes blue and red Digitized Sky Survey 2 data. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, revealing the texture of the dark cloud and faint light around the young stars.
